1167630.note: Teardown's physics and lighting lean hard on both the CPU and GPU, and big explosions always dip. Render Scale helps the most.

settings.name: Render Scale
settings.why: Draws fewer pixels. The biggest single gain.

settings.name: Render Quality
settings.why: Lighting detail, and heavy on Macs.

settings.name: Particles
settings.why: Smoke and debris cost most when things explode.

settings.name: Upscaling
settings.why: Try AMD FSR on Performance if it's still slow. It hasn't been tested on a Mac here.

settings.name: Vsync
settings.why: Below 60 fps, vsync can hold you down to 30.

settings.name: Motion Blur
settings.why: Hides less than it costs at lower frame rates.

settings.name: Depth of Field
settings.why: A small saving for little visual loss.

1118200.note: People Playground is limited by physics, so big scenes slow down on any Mac. Clearing debris and corpses helps more than any graphics option.

settings.name: Collision Quality
settings.why: Saves physics work when a scene gets crowded.

settings.name: Physics Iterations
settings.why: The heaviest setting here. Lower is less accurate but much faster.

settings.name: Bloom
settings.why: An effect you can drop with little visual loss.

settings.name: Fancy Effects
settings.why: Extra visual effects that add up in big scenes.

settings.name: Decals
settings.why: Part of the game's look. Turn off only if blood builds up and slows things.

settings.name: Procedural Fragments
settings.why: Breaking things into pieces creates more physics work.

settings.name: Framerate Limit
settings.why: A limit saves heat and battery, and this Mac's screen may not show more.

4000.note: Addons usually matter more than graphics in Garry's Mod. Unsubscribing from ones you don't use is the best fix. Garry's Mod also has a real Mac version in Steam.

settings.name: Model Detail
settings.why: Matters most on servers with many players.

settings.name: Texture Detail
settings.why: Uses memory more than speed.

settings.name: Shader Detail
settings.why: A cheap way to gain frames.

settings.name: Water Detail
settings.why: Costly on maps with water.

settings.name: Shadow Detail
settings.why: A cheap way to gain frames.

settings.name: Antialiasing Mode
settings.why: Costly, and the screen is already sharp.

settings.name: Multicore Rendering
settings.why: Spreads work across cores. Turn it off if the game crashes.

2168680.note: This covers only the options Cellar could confirm from the game's saved settings, and the names in its menu may differ slightly. Big online matches get slower as they go, which players often put down to smoke, though that isn't confirmed.

settings.name: FPS Limit
settings.why: Keeps a fanless Mac cooler and steadier.

settings.name: Grass
settings.why: Lots of small objects, especially at low altitude.

settings.name: Texture Quality
settings.why: Saves memory on smaller Macs.

settings.name: Vsync
settings.why: Below 60 fps, vsync can hold you down to 30. Use the limit instead.

3892270.note: A small co-op game, so a frame limit mostly saves heat and battery.

settings.name: Quality
settings.why: The game's main graphics setting.

settings.name: Max Frame Rate
settings.why: It's on Unlimited by default, which runs the Mac flat out for nothing.

settings.name: Vsync
settings.why: Use the frame limit instead.

settings.name: Anisotropic Filtering
settings.why: Cheap sharpness on floors at an angle.

settings.name: Film Grain
settings.why: Taste. It costs almost nothing.
